title: Vertical spindle moulder
description: The vertical spindle moulder is one of the most versatile machines in woodworking. It can be used for mouldings, rebates and curved work. However, due to the risk of contact with the tool, and ejection of the tool part or workpiece, it can be hazardous if not used correctly.

title: Thicknessers (surface & thicknessers, under and over planers)
description: Thicknessing machines are mainly used on timber that has already been straightened on a surface planer.

title: Tenoners
description: A tenon is the end of timber shaped to fit in a mortise and make a joint.

title: Rise fall saws
description: A rise and fall saw follows a cycle of operations until the cut is complete. A clamp holds timber against the table, while a circular blade lifts to cut through it. Once the cut is complete, the blade retracts, the clamp lifts, and the timber can be moved, ready for the next cycle.

title: Worker engagement and participation
description: Health and safety legislation requires employers to engage workers in the whole risk management process. Information Sheet.

title: Radial arm saws
description: A radial arm saw is a circular saw mounted on a sliding horizontal arm. It is often used for cutting long pieces of timber to length.

title: Pendulum saws (swing saws, cut-off trim saws)
description: Pendulum saws have a frame suspended from a shaft over the work table, and are fitted with a single circular crosscut blade. A handle on the saw frame enables the operator to draw it forward when making a cut.

title: Overhand planing machines
description: Named for the position of the hands of the operator, an overhand planing machine is a horizontal cylindrical cutter block set between two tables, with knives secured in the cutter block. It is sometimes called a “jointer”.

title: Mitre saws
description: A mitre saw is a circular saw mounted on a frame, fixed to a rotating cutting table to make various cuts across the grain of timber. The saw may have a slide action, allowing cuts on much wider boards. Without a slide action, it is also known as a chop saw, or cut-off saw.

title: Mortisers
description: A mortise is a hole cut in timber to receive a tenon and make a joint. This factsheet focuses on floor-mounted and bench-mounted machines found in factories, specifically on the safety of mortisers used to make rectangular holes.

title: Horizontal beam and vertical panel saws
description: Horizontal beam panel saws are used to cut panels into pieces and it can cut multiple panels at the same time.

title: Four siders
description: Also known as a timber moulding machine, a four sider has at least four cutting heads so it can machine and shape long sides of timber in one pass.

title: Circular saw benches
description: Circular saws (including sliding table dimensioning saws and tilting arbor saws) are useful tools to quickly cut timber, chipboard or MDF. Some circular saws can also cut concrete and masonry.

title: Rotary printing press
description: A rotary printing press is a press in which paper or other materials receive images from a rubber coated cylinder, called the blanket or offset cylinder.

title: Platen press
description: A platen press is a printing press in which paper or other material, supported on flat impression surfaces, is forced against printing surfaces that are supported on stationary flat beds. This includes creasing and scoring presses of the platen type.
